mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 1% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 0.5% signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < -0.5% AND HOUST < -0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 per month for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a simultaneous rise in the producer price index (not available, so use CPIAUCSL as proxy for inflationary pressure) above 2.5% signals cost-push inflation and supply chain stress, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -0.5% AND CPIAUCSL > 2.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
